shots.say: Why does a monkey have such a long tail?
Is it a toy? A scarf? Or a hand?
I'm Milo. Let's find out together!
Welcome to The Animated Zoo, friends!
Today we fly up to the rainforest treetops.
Here we are! Look who is sitting on the branch.
This is Mango. Mango is a spider monkey.
Hello, Mango! Look behind her. What a long tail!
It curls, and wiggles, and swishes!
Do you have a tail? Wiggle, wiggle!
Let's measure. Mango stands up tall. This is her body.
And this is her tail, stretched out next to her.
Which one is longer? Her body, or her tail?
Her tail! A spider monkey's tail is longer than its body.
Wow! Can you stretch out long, like a tail? Stretch!
But what does Mango do with her long tail? Watch!
She wraps it around the branch, and down she goes!
Her tail holds on tight. Squeeze!
A spider monkey's tail can grab, and hold on.
Round and round the branch it goes.
It holds on, just like an extra hand!
Can you grab with your hand? Squeeze, squeeze!
Let's count what Mango can hold on with.
One hand, two hands,
one foot, two feet,
and her long tail. Five!
How many can Mango hold on with? Four, or five?
Five! Two hands, two feet, and one tail.
Mango has five ways to hold on!
How many hands do you have? Show me!
Look! A tree full of golden fruit.
Mango hangs upside down, just by her tail!
Spider monkeys spend most of the day high up in the treetops.
They climb, and swing, from branch to branch.
Sometimes spider monkeys hang by their tails just to play!
What do you like to play?
A spider monkey's tail can hold up its whole body.
Can you tilt your head, like Mango? Tilt!
Now both of her hands are free. What will she do?
Can Mango pick fruit while she hangs? Yes, or no?
Yes! One fruit, two fruits. Both hands are busy!
Count the fruits with me. One, two!
Her tail holds on, so her hands can pick, and eat.
Two hands for fruit, and one tail to hold on.
Munch, munch! A snack, upside down!
Pretend to munch a fruit with me. Yum!
Do you know why she is called a spider monkey?
When she hangs, her long arms and legs dangle down.
Hello, upside-down Mango!
Long arms, long legs, a little bit like a spider!
That is how the spider monkey got its name!
Can you wiggle your arms like a spider monkey?
Mango swings over to a tree full of flowers.
Look closely at the very tip of her tail.
Under the tip, there are little lines.
Now look at your fingertip. You have little lines, too!
Your little lines are only yours!
Here are three spider monkey tails. One, two, three.
Every spider monkey has its own lines. Look, all different!
Are Mango's lines the same as her friend's? Yes, or no?
No! Mango's lines are only Mango's.
And the little lines help her tail hold on tight.
Her tail holds the branch, tight, tight, tight!
Her hands are good at holding, too. Four long fingers!
They hook onto a branch. Hook!
Can you make a hook with your fingers? Hook!
Hands that hook, and a tail that grabs. Just right for the treetops!
Look who is here! Mango's friend Coco, and her baby.
The baby wraps its tiny tail around its mama's tail.
That helps the baby feel safe and snug.
Hold on tight, little baby!
Who do you hold hands with?
Can you give yourself a big hug? Squeeze!
What a wonderful tail, Mango!
Time to remember what we learned!
Which is longer? Mango's body, or her tail?
What can her tail do? Hold on, or sing?
Hold on! Just like an extra hand.
What is under the tip of her tail?
Little lines, just like your fingertip!
Good night, Mango. Hold on tight!
Thank you for learning with me, friends. See you at the zoo!
